Clean author names with Scopus author IDs and ORCID

Source: R/authors_clean.R
authors_clean.Rd

Rewrites the author field of a bibliometric data frame so that each person has one spelling and different people never share one. Identity comes from IDs only, never from names:

* all spellings of one Scopus ID become one spelling (the most frequent, then the most recent, then the longest), with the accents kept; * with `openalex = TRUE`, OpenAlex is asked by DOI for each author's ORCID, and Scopus IDs whose papers carry the same ORCID are joined into one person. An author without a usable Scopus ID takes its OpenAlex author ID; * different people who share a spelling stay apart, labelled `"KIM J"`, `"KIM J (2)"`, ... by number of papers; * an author identified by neither source keeps its spelling, and a paper with no identified author is left untouched.

A merge whose spellings do not look like one name ("ENDRASS B" and "LUGRIN B" under one Scopus ID) is kept but flagged `check = TRUE`. Lost accents ("KRMER N"), initials against given names ("MOORE RL", "MOORE ROBERT L") and a surname part dropped ("LOPEZ SS", "SAFFON LOPEZ S") count as one name. Write the merges to a file with [review_sheet()], mark the ones that are wrong `split`, and pass the file back as `review`.

Scopus writes a generational suffix as its own name ("Huff E.W., Jr."), and names may hold HTML entities (`L&#x00F3;pez`); both are repaired.

Usage

authors_clean(
  data,
  scopus = NULL,
  author_ids = "Author(s) ID",
  eid = "eid",
  authors = "AU",
  doi = "DI",
  year = "PY",
  openalex = TRUE,
  mailto = NULL,
  review = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per paper, such as a bibliometrix data frame. The result of another `clean_*()` function works too, so the cleaners chain: `M |> authors_clean(scopus = "Dlds") |> keywords_clean()`.

scopus

Paths to the raw Scopus CSV exports, or a folder holding them. They need the columns `Authors`, `Author(s) ID`, `DOI` and `EID`. Leave it out when `data` itself holds the Scopus author IDs (column `author_ids`): bibliometrix drops them, so a bibliometrix data frame needs `scopus`. Given both, `scopus` is used, since its names keep their accents.

author_ids

Name of the column in `data` holding the Scopus author IDs (`;`-separated, in the order of the authors), read when `scopus` is left out. Default `"Author(s) ID"`, Scopus's own name.

eid

Name of the column in `data` holding the Scopus EID (`"2-s2.0-..."`), which links each paper to its Scopus row.

authors, doi, year

Names of the author (`;`-separated), DOI and publication-year columns in `data`. The defaults are bibliometrix's.

openalex

Logical. Consult OpenAlex for the gaps described above? Needs the httr2 package and an internet connection. Default `TRUE`.

mailto

Optional e-mail address sent to OpenAlex to use its polite pool. Default `NULL` sends none.

review

Optional reviewed merges: the `.csv` or `.xlsx` file from [review_sheet()], or a data frame with its columns `person_key` and `decision`. A person marked `split` is taken apart again: into its Scopus IDs when ORCID joined several, otherwise into its Scopus spellings. An empty `decision` or `keep` keeps the merge. Default `NULL`.

Value

A `saqr_authors` object:

  • `as.data.frame(x)`: `data` with the author column rewritten and a new `AU_ID` column holding the matching person keys in the same order (`-` for an unidentified author; `NA` for an untouched paper).

  • [authors_changes()]: one row per person whose spelling changed, who was joined across Scopus IDs, or who shares a spelling, most papers first: `person_key`, `name`, `spellings`, `papers`, `scopus_ids`, `merged` (one Scopus ID, several spellings), `check` (a merged or joined person whose spellings do not look like one name), `homonym`, `orcid_conflict` (the person's papers show more than one ORCID; flagged, not split) and `split` (a part of a person `review` took apart; a part split by spelling has the key `<key>|<spelling>`). [authors_check()] gives its rows with `check = TRUE`.

  • `as.data.frame(x, what = "authors")`: one row per author per paper (for tracing a single decision): `eid`, `doi`, `year`, `position`, `name_before`, `name_scopus`, `scopus_id`, `openalex_id`, `orcid`, `person_key` (`scopus:<id>`, `orcid:<id>`, `openalex:<id>`, or `NA`), `split_from` (the key `review` split, else `NA`), `source` and `name`.

`summary()` returns the counts as a data frame.

Errors

Raises `saqrmisc_bad_input` when `data` lacks a named column, has repeated EIDs, `scopus` names no readable Scopus export, or `review` is not a review sheet or holds a decision other than `keep` or `split`; `saqrmisc_missing_package` when `openalex = TRUE` without httr2, or for an `.xlsx` `review` without readxl. A `saqrmisc_review_unmatched` warning names reviewed people this run does not have. A `saqrmisc_openalex_failed` warning reports OpenAlex requests that failed; the authors involved keep their Scopus identity.

References

Priem, J., Piwowar, H., & Orr, R. (2022). OpenAlex: A fully-open index of scholarly works, authors, venues, institutions, and concepts. arXiv:2205.01833.

Baas, J., Schotten, M., Plume, A., Côté, G., & Karimi, R. (2020). Scopus as a curated, high-quality bibliometric data source for academic research in quantitative science studies. *Quantitative Science Studies*, 1(1), 377-386. doi:10.1162/qss_a_00019

Examples

scopus_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(data.frame(
  Authors = c("Pérez-Marín D., Kim J.", "Perez-Marin D., Kim J."),
  `Author(s) ID` = c("111;201;", "111;202;"),
  DOI = c("10.1/a", "10.1/b"),
  EID = c("2-s2.0-1", "2-s2.0-2"),
  check.names = FALSE
), scopus_file, row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
papers <- data.frame(
  eid = c("2-s2.0-1", "2-s2.0-2"),
  AU = c("PREZ-MARN D;KIM J", "PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J"),
  DI = c("10.1/a", "10.1/b"),
  PY = c(2019, 2020)
)
cleaned <- authors_clean(papers, scopus = scopus_file, openalex = FALSE)
cleaned
#> Author cleaning by Scopus ID
#>   2 of 2 papers rewritten; 3 people
#>   1 Scopus IDs had several spellings, now one; 0 people joined across Scopus IDs by ORCID
#>   0 of these merges to check: their spellings do not look like one name
#>   2 share a spelling and are numbered; 0 ORCID conflicts flagged
#>   0 author rows unidentified, kept as they were
#> 
#> as.data.frame(x) gives the cleaned papers; review_sheet(x, file) writes every merge for you to check.
as.data.frame(cleaned)
#>        eid                      AU     DI   PY                 AU_ID
#> 1 2-s2.0-1     PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J 10.1/a 2019 scopus:111;scopus:201
#> 2 2-s2.0-2 PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J (2) 10.1/b 2020 scopus:111;scopus:202
authors_changes(cleaned)
#>   person_key          name                   spellings papers scopus_ids merged
#> 1 scopus:111 PEREZ-MARIN D PEREZ-MARIN D | PREZ-MARN D      2          1   TRUE
#> 2 scopus:201         KIM J                       KIM J      1          1  FALSE
#> 3 scopus:202     KIM J (2)                       KIM J      1          1  FALSE
#>   check homonym orcid_conflict split
#> 1 FALSE   FALSE          FALSE FALSE
#> 2 FALSE    TRUE          FALSE FALSE
#> 3 FALSE    TRUE          FALSE FALSE

# Merges to check go to a file; mark a wrong one `split` and pass it back.
sheet <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
review_sheet(cleaned, sheet)
#> file21ed4b2d8722.csv: 1 merge(s), 0 to check. Write split in decision for a wrong one, then authors_clean(review = "file21ed4b2d8722.csv").
undone <- authors_clean(papers, scopus = scopus_file, openalex = FALSE,
                        review = data.frame(person_key = "scopus:111", decision = "split"))
as.data.frame(undone)
#>        eid                      AU     DI   PY
#> 1 2-s2.0-1     PÉREZ-MARÍN D;KIM J 10.1/a 2019
#> 2 2-s2.0-2 PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J (2) 10.1/b 2020
#>                                 AU_ID
#> 1 scopus:111|PÉREZ-MARÍN D;scopus:201
#> 2 scopus:111|PEREZ-MARIN D;scopus:202
